items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Roger's place was my hangout, and although I could not speak very much French, and he spoke no English, we made ourselves understood.

ctx.x: I was being paid by the week but was only working Sunday afternoons, because the new club that I had been engaged to play in was to be in the Eduuard 7th theatre building and had not been finished to open when I arrived. I had not heard any outstanding trumpet players or musicians, except the ones I was working with during my first two weeks in Paris.

Thirteen days after my arrival in Paris, Christmas came and then I got the blues, because I had not made the acquaintance of anyone that may have invited me to join them in celebrating the holidays, and the few people that I knew were spending that time with their families. So I passed the time in a bar at the corner of rue Fontaine and rue Douai, owned by an ex-prize fighter named Roger. The same thing went for New Years. I drank 1948 out and 1949 in. Roger's place was my hangout, and although I could not speak…

One night just before Christmas, I was in this bar and somone tapped me on the back. I turned to see who it was and had a great surprise when I looked into the face of Joe Turner, the pianist. Joe had been in France and other parts of Europe before the last war, and we had met in Boudon's many times. He was surprised to see me also, because he didn't know that I was back in France. I had not seen him around New York for quite a while before I left. It certainly was nice seeing a fellow musician from across the…
